description: Decompose a signal into its frequency components: window and transform the data, identify spectral peaks, estimate power spectral density, filter target bands, and validate against the time-domain signal.

steps.description: Prepare the raw signal for spectral analysis: check sampling rate, detrend, handle gaps, and apply a window function.

inputs.name: raw-signal
inputs.desc: The time-domain signal with timestamps and values

inputs.name: sampling-metadata
inputs.desc: Sampling rate, units, known gaps, and recording conditions

outputs.name: windowed-signal
outputs.desc: Preprocessed signal ready for transform

outputs.name: preprocessing-log
outputs.desc: Steps taken: detrending method, window type, gap handling

process: Verify the sampling rate matches metadata and check for irregular spacing.
Remove any DC offset and linear trend from the signal.
Handle gaps by interpolation or segmentation depending on gap length.
Apply a window function (Hanning, Hamming, or Blackman) to reduce spectral leakage.

steps.description: Compute the frequency-domain representation using FFT or related transform, producing amplitude and phase spectra.

inputs.name: transform-parameters
inputs.desc: FFT size, overlap, zero-padding, and transform type

outputs.name: amplitude-spectrum
outputs.desc: Magnitude at each frequency bin

outputs.name: phase-spectrum
outputs.desc: Phase angle at each frequency bin

process: Choose the FFT size (next power of 2 or zero-padded).
Compute the discrete Fourier transform of the windowed signal.
Convert complex output to amplitude (magnitude) and phase.
Scale the amplitude spectrum to physical units (e.g., amplitude spectral density).

steps.description: Identify significant peaks in the amplitude spectrum: locate frequency, amplitude, bandwidth, and signal-to-noise ratio of each peak.

inputs.name: noise-floor-estimate
inputs.desc: Expected background noise level or method to estimate it

outputs.name: peak-table
outputs.desc: Each peak with frequency, amplitude, bandwidth, and SNR

outputs.name: noise-floor
outputs.desc: The estimated noise floor used for SNR calculation

process: Estimate the noise floor using a moving median or percentile method.
Find local maxima that exceed the noise floor by a specified threshold.
For each peak, measure the center frequency, amplitude, and 3dB bandwidth.
Compute the signal-to-noise ratio for each peak.

steps.description: Estimate the power spectral density using Welch's method or a multitaper approach for a smooth, unbiased estimate.

inputs.name: estimation-parameters
inputs.desc: Segment length, overlap fraction, taper count

outputs.name: psd-estimate
outputs.desc: Power spectral density with frequency axis and confidence bounds

outputs.name: spectral-resolution
outputs.desc: Frequency resolution and bandwidth of the estimate

process: Divide the signal into overlapping segments.
Compute the periodogram of each segment (or apply multiple tapers).
Average across segments to reduce variance.
Compute confidence intervals based on the number of independent segments.

steps.description: Design and apply a bandpass filter to isolate a target frequency band, then convert back to time domain.

inputs.name: target-band
inputs.desc: The frequency range to extract (low cutoff, high cutoff)

outputs.name: filtered-signal
outputs.desc: Time-domain signal containing only the target band

outputs.name: filter-specification
outputs.desc: Filter type, order, cutoff frequencies, and rolloff

process: Design a bandpass filter with the specified cutoff frequencies.
Choose filter type (Butterworth, Chebyshev, or FIR) based on rolloff needs.
Apply the filter using zero-phase (forward-backward) filtering to avoid phase distortion.
Verify the filtered output by checking its spectrum against the target band.

steps.description: Compile the spectral analysis results into a structured report: dominant frequencies, spectral shape, filtered components, and interpretation.

outputs.name: spectral-report
outputs.desc: Structured analysis report with figures and interpretation

outputs.name: frequency-summary
outputs.desc: Table of dominant frequencies and their physical interpretation

process: Summarize the dominant spectral peaks and their physical meaning.
Describe the overall spectral shape (broadband vs narrowband, colored noise type).
Present the filtered component and its time-domain behavior.
Note any unexpected features or artifacts found during the analysis.

description: Fit dose-response curves from experimental data: organize the data, select candidate models, fit curves, extract potency parameters (EC50/IC50), assess model adequacy, and compare treatments.

steps.description: Organize raw dose-response data: log-transform concentrations, normalize responses, flag outliers, and structure for fitting.

inputs.name: assay-metadata
inputs.desc: Units, vehicle control values, positive control values, assay type

outputs.name: organized-data
outputs.desc: Cleaned data with log-concentrations, normalized responses, and replicate structure

outputs.name: normalization-record
outputs.desc: How normalization was done (0% and 100% reference points)

process: Log-transform concentrations (base 10 or natural log, stated explicitly).
Normalize responses to the vehicle control (0%) and positive control (100%).
Flag statistical outliers within replicate groups using Grubbs test or similar.
Structure the data as columns: log_concentration, response, replicate_id, treatment_group.

steps.description: Select candidate dose-response models: 4-parameter logistic (4PL), 5-parameter logistic (5PL), or log-logistic, based on the data shape.

inputs.name: prior-knowledge
inputs.desc: Whether the curve is expected to be symmetric, whether bottom/top plateaus are known

outputs.name: candidate-models
outputs.desc: List of models to fit, with their parameter definitions

outputs.name: initial-guesses
outputs.desc: Starting parameter values for each model derived from the data

process: Inspect the data for asymmetry (suggesting 5PL over 4PL).
Determine whether to fix the bottom asymptote at 0% and the top at 100% or estimate them.
List the candidate models with their equations and free parameters.
Estimate initial parameter guesses from the data (midpoint for EC50, slope from the steepest segment).

steps.description: Fit each candidate model to the data using nonlinear least squares or maximum likelihood, reporting parameter estimates with standard errors.

outputs.name: fit-results
outputs.desc: For each model: parameter estimates, standard errors, and goodness-of-fit statistics

outputs.name: convergence-log
outputs.desc: Whether each fit converged and any issues encountered

process: Fit each candidate model using weighted nonlinear least squares (weights from replicate variance).
Record parameter estimates, their standard errors, and confidence intervals.
Compute goodness-of-fit: R-squared, residual standard error, AIC, and BIC.
Check convergence and parameter identifiability (are confidence intervals finite?).

steps.description: Extract the key potency parameters from the fitted model: EC50/IC50, Hill slope, maximum effect, and minimum effect.

outputs.name: potency-table
outputs.desc: EC50/IC50 with confidence interval, Hill slope, Emax, Emin for each model

outputs.name: dose-at-effect
outputs.desc: Inverse prediction: concentration needed for specific effect levels (e.g., EC90)

process: Extract EC50 (or IC50 for inhibition) directly from the fitted midpoint parameter.
Compute the confidence interval for EC50 using the delta method or profile likelihood.
Back-calculate concentrations for other effect levels (EC10, EC90) from the fitted curve.
Report the Hill coefficient and its interpretation (steepness of the transition).

steps.description: Check whether the fitted model is adequate: residual analysis, lack-of-fit test, and comparison of candidate models.

outputs.name: adequacy-report
outputs.desc: Residual plots, lack-of-fit test result, model comparison (AIC/BIC)

outputs.name: selected-model
outputs.desc: The best model and why it was chosen

process: Plot residuals vs. fitted values and vs. concentration to check for patterns.
Run a lack-of-fit test (compare pure error to model residuals using replicate data).
Compare candidate models using AIC or likelihood ratio test if nested.
Select the simplest model that passes the lack-of-fit test.

steps.description: Compare dose-response curves across treatments: test whether EC50 values differ, whether curves are parallel, and whether maximum effects differ.

inputs.name: potency-table
inputs.desc: EC50 and curve parameters for each treatment

inputs.name: fit-results
inputs.desc: Full fit details for statistical comparison

outputs.name: comparison-results
outputs.desc: Statistical tests for EC50 differences, parallelism, and Emax differences

outputs.name: potency-ratios
outputs.desc: Relative potency ratios with confidence intervals

process: Test whether EC50 values differ between treatments (extra-sum-of-squares F-test).
Test whether curves are parallel (same Hill slope) by constraining and comparing fits.
If parallel, compute the relative potency ratio and its confidence interval.
Test whether maximum effects differ by comparing Emax parameters.

description: Analyze time-to-event data: prepare the dataset with censoring indicators, estimate survival curves, compare groups, fit regression models, check assumptions, and report results.

steps.description: Prepare the survival dataset: define the time variable, the event indicator, and the censoring mechanism.

inputs.name: raw-dataset
inputs.desc: Subject-level data with dates or times and event status

inputs.name: study-design
inputs.desc: Start point, endpoint definition, censoring rules, and follow-up window

outputs.name: survival-dataset
outputs.desc: Cleaned dataset with time, event (0/1), and covariates

outputs.name: censoring-summary
outputs.desc: Number and proportion censored, reasons for censoring

process: Define time zero (enrollment, diagnosis, randomization) for each subject.
Calculate time to event or censoring from time zero.
Code the event indicator: 1 for the event, 0 for censored observations.
Classify censoring reasons (end of study, loss to follow-up, competing event).

steps.description: Estimate the survival function using the Kaplan-Meier method: step function, confidence bands, and median survival time.

inputs.name: survival-dataset
inputs.desc: Time, event indicator, and group variable

inputs.name: confidence-level
inputs.desc: Desired confidence level for the survival bands (e.g., 95%)

outputs.name: km-curves
outputs.desc: Kaplan-Meier survival curves by group with confidence bands

outputs.name: km-summary
outputs.desc: Median survival, restricted mean survival time, and survival at landmark times

process: Compute the KM estimator: product of conditional survival probabilities at each event time.
Compute Greenwood confidence intervals at each time point.
Extract the median survival time (where the curve crosses 0.50) with its CI.
Report survival probability at clinically relevant landmark times.

steps.description: Compare survival curves between groups using the log-rank test and its variants.

inputs.name: test-variant
inputs.desc: Standard log-rank, Wilcoxon (Peto-Prentice), or stratified log-rank

outputs.name: logrank-result
outputs.desc: Test statistic, degrees of freedom, and p-value

outputs.name: hazard-ratio-estimate
outputs.desc: Unadjusted hazard ratio from the log-rank framework

process: Select the appropriate test variant based on the expected hazard pattern.
Compute observed and expected events per group at each event time.
Calculate the test statistic and its p-value.
Estimate the unadjusted hazard ratio from the O/E ratio.

steps.description: Fit a Cox proportional hazards model: estimate hazard ratios for covariates, test significance, and extract the baseline hazard.

inputs.name: covariate-specification
inputs.desc: Which covariates to include and how (continuous, categorical, interaction)

outputs.name: cox-model
outputs.desc: Fitted model with hazard ratios, confidence intervals, and p-values

outputs.name: model-fit-statistics
outputs.desc: Concordance index, likelihood ratio test, and Wald test

process: Specify the model formula with covariates and any interaction or stratification terms.
Fit the Cox model using partial likelihood estimation.
Extract hazard ratios with 95% confidence intervals for each covariate.
Compute the concordance index as a measure of discrimination.

steps.description: Check the proportional hazards assumption: Schoenfeld residual tests, log-log plots, and time-varying covariate analysis.

outputs.name: ph-test-results
outputs.desc: Schoenfeld residual tests for each covariate and globally

outputs.name: remediation-plan
outputs.desc: If PH is violated, recommended fixes (stratification, time-varying, or parametric model)

process: Compute scaled Schoenfeld residuals and test for a non-zero slope over time.
Plot log(-log(S(t))) curves by group to visually check for parallelism.
If violation is detected, identify which covariate(s) violate and at what time range.
Recommend a fix: stratify on the violating variable, add a time interaction, or switch to a parametric model.

steps.description: Write the survival analysis report: KM curves, group comparisons, Cox model results, assumption diagnostics, and clinical interpretation.

outputs.name: survival-report
outputs.desc: Structured report with tables, figures, and interpretation

outputs.name: key-findings
outputs.desc: One-paragraph summary of the main survival findings

process: Present the KM curves with number-at-risk tables below.
Report the Cox model results in a standard table format.
Summarize the PH diagnostics and any model modifications made.
Write the interpretation: what the results mean for the research question.

description: Analyze spatial data: map point patterns, test for clustering, estimate spatial autocorrelation, interpolate with kriging, and produce spatial prediction maps with uncertainty.

steps.description: Map the spatial data: project coordinates, define the study region boundary, and compute basic spatial statistics.

inputs.name: spatial-dataset
inputs.desc: Observations with coordinates (x,y or lat/lon) and measured values

inputs.name: region-definition
inputs.desc: Study area boundary (polygon) and coordinate reference system

outputs.name: projected-dataset
outputs.desc: Observations in a projected coordinate system with distances in meters

outputs.name: spatial-summary
outputs.desc: Point count, spatial extent, mean nearest-neighbor distance, and intensity

process: Project the coordinates to a local metric CRS if they are in geographic (lat/lon).
Clip observations to the study region boundary.
Compute basic spatial statistics: intensity (points per area), mean nearest-neighbor distance.
Produce a map of the study region with observation locations.

steps.description: Test for spatial clustering: Ripley's K function, nearest-neighbor index, or quadrat test to determine if the pattern departs from randomness.

outputs.name: clustering-result
outputs.desc: Test statistic and whether the pattern is clustered, dispersed, or random

outputs.name: scale-dependence
outputs.desc: At what spatial scales clustering or dispersion is strongest

process: Compute Ripley's K function across a range of distances.
Compare observed K to the expected K under complete spatial randomness (CSR).
Identify the distances at which the pattern most deviates from CSR.
Run a significance test using Monte Carlo simulation of CSR envelopes.

steps.description: Estimate spatial autocorrelation in the measured values: compute the variogram, fit a variogram model, and extract range, sill, and nugget parameters.

inputs.name: projected-dataset
inputs.desc: Observations with coordinates and measured values

inputs.name: lag-parameters
inputs.desc: Maximum lag distance, bin width, and directional anisotropy checks

outputs.name: empirical-variogram
outputs.desc: Semivariance vs. lag distance with bin counts

outputs.name: fitted-variogram
outputs.desc: Model parameters: nugget, sill, range, and model type (spherical, exponential, Gaussian)

process: Compute the empirical variogram: mean squared differences of pairs at each lag bin.
Check for anisotropy by computing directional variograms.
Fit candidate variogram models (spherical, exponential, Gaussian) using weighted least squares.
Select the best model and extract the nugget (measurement error), sill (total variance), and range (correlation distance).

steps.description: Interpolate the measured values across the study region using ordinary or universal kriging, producing predictions and kriging variance at unsampled locations.

inputs.name: fitted-variogram
inputs.desc: The variogram model to use for kriging weights

outputs.name: prediction-surface
outputs.desc: Interpolated values on a regular grid covering the study region

outputs.name: kriging-variance
outputs.desc: Prediction uncertainty at each grid cell

process: Define the prediction grid covering the study region at the desired resolution.
For each grid cell, solve the kriging system to obtain weights for nearby observations.
Compute the kriging prediction (weighted combination of nearby observations).
Compute the kriging variance (prediction uncertainty that increases away from data points).

steps.description: Validate the spatial model using leave-one-out cross-validation: compare predicted values to withheld observations and compute accuracy metrics.

outputs.name: cv-metrics
outputs.desc: Mean error, mean absolute error, RMSE, and standardized prediction error

outputs.name: cv-diagnostics
outputs.desc: Scatter plot of predicted vs. observed and spatial map of residuals

process: Remove one observation at a time and predict its value from the remaining data.
Compute the prediction error and the standardized error (error / kriging standard deviation).
Calculate summary metrics: ME (should be near zero), MAE, RMSE.
Check that standardized errors have mean near 0 and variance near 1 (model is well-calibrated).

steps.description: Produce the spatial analysis report: maps, variogram analysis, prediction surface, uncertainty map, and interpretation.

outputs.name: spatial-report
outputs.desc: Structured report with maps, statistics, and interpretation

outputs.name: data-collection-guidance
outputs.desc: Where to sample next to reduce prediction uncertainty

process: Present the observation map, prediction map, and uncertainty map side by side.
Summarize the variogram analysis: correlation range, nugget ratio, and anisotropy.
Report validation metrics and whether the model is adequately calibrated.
Identify high-uncertainty areas and recommend additional sampling locations.

description: Analyze a factorial experiment: encode the design matrix, compute main effects and interactions, test significance, generate response surface plots, and identify optimal factor settings.

steps.description: Encode the factorial design: list factors and levels, build the coded design matrix, and verify the design structure (full or fractional, resolution).

inputs.name: factor-definitions
inputs.desc: Each factor with its name, levels, and coded values

inputs.name: experimental-results
inputs.desc: Response values for each run in the design

outputs.name: design-matrix
outputs.desc: Coded design matrix with factors, interactions, and response columns

outputs.name: design-properties
outputs.desc: Number of factors, levels, runs, resolution, and aliasing structure

process: List all factors with their low (-1) and high (+1) coded levels.
Build the full design matrix including all main effects and interactions.
If fractional, identify the generators and the aliasing structure.
Verify that the response column has the correct number of observations per run.

steps.description: Calculate main effects and interaction effects: the average change in response when each factor moves from low to high.

outputs.name: effect-estimates
outputs.desc: Each effect (main and interaction) with its magnitude and sign

outputs.name: effect-ranking
outputs.desc: Effects sorted by absolute magnitude

process: Compute each main effect: average response at high level minus average at low level.
Compute each interaction effect: half the difference of a factor's effect at the other factor's levels.
For higher-order interactions, apply the sign-table method.
Rank effects by absolute magnitude to identify the most influential factors.

steps.description: Test which effects are statistically significant: ANOVA, normal probability plot of effects, or Lenth's method for unreplicated designs.

inputs.name: design-properties
inputs.desc: Whether the design is replicated or unreplicated

outputs.name: anova-table
outputs.desc: Source, sum of squares, df, mean square, F-ratio, and p-value for each effect

outputs.name: significant-effects
outputs.desc: Effects that pass the significance threshold

process: If replicated, use ANOVA with pure error from replicates.
If unreplicated, use a normal probability plot of effects or Lenth's pseudo-standard-error.
Compute the F-ratio and p-value for each effect.
Apply a multiple-comparison correction if testing many effects simultaneously.

steps.description: Generate contour and surface plots of the response as a function of the two most important factors, with other factors held at their center or optimal values.

outputs.name: surface-plots
outputs.desc: Contour and 3D surface plots for the top factor pairs

outputs.name: response-model
outputs.desc: Fitted polynomial model of the response surface

process: Fit a polynomial model (linear + interactions, or quadratic if center points exist).
Select the two most influential factors for the primary plot.
Generate a contour plot and a 3D surface plot of predicted response.
If more than two factors are significant, produce additional plots with non-focal factors held constant.

steps.description: Find the factor settings that optimize the response: steepest ascent direction, predicted optimum within the design space, and confidence region around it.

outputs.name: optimal-settings
outputs.desc: Factor levels that maximize or minimize the response

outputs.name: predicted-optimum
outputs.desc: Predicted response at the optimal settings with confidence interval

process: If the optimum is within the design region, solve for the stationary point of the response model.
If the optimum is outside (first-order model), compute the steepest ascent direction.
Apply any constraints on factor ranges.
Report the optimal settings and the predicted response with its uncertainty.

steps.description: Compile the factorial experiment report: design summary, effect estimates, significance tests, response surfaces, optimal settings, and recommendations.

outputs.name: factorial-report
outputs.desc: Structured report of the factorial analysis

outputs.name: next-experiment-recommendation
outputs.desc: Whether to run additional experiments (augment, center points, response surface)

process: Summarize the design: factors, levels, runs, and resolution.
Present the effect estimates with the Pareto chart and ANOVA table.
Show the response surface plots for the key factor pairs.
Recommend the optimal settings and whether follow-up experiments are needed.

description: Combine data from multiple sensors into a single estimate: align sensor timelines, characterize each sensor's noise, compute optimal fusion weights, fuse with a Kalman-style approach, and validate the fused output.

steps.description: Align the time axes of multiple sensors: handle different sampling rates, clock offsets, and latency differences.

inputs.name: multi-sensor-data
inputs.desc: Data streams from each sensor with timestamps and values

inputs.name: sensor-specifications
inputs.desc: Sampling rates, latencies, and known clock offsets for each sensor

outputs.name: aligned-data
outputs.desc: All sensor streams resampled to a common time axis

outputs.name: alignment-log
outputs.desc: Clock corrections applied, interpolation method used, and samples lost

process: Identify the common time window covered by all sensors.
Apply known clock offsets and latency corrections.
Resample each sensor to a common time grid using appropriate interpolation.
Flag periods where any sensor has gaps exceeding its Nyquist interval.

steps.description: Characterize each sensor's noise: estimate its variance, spectral profile, and any systematic biases.

inputs.name: reference-data
inputs.desc: A known reference or a period where the true value is constant, if available

outputs.name: noise-profiles
outputs.desc: Each sensor's noise variance, spectral shape, and bias estimate

outputs.name: correlation-matrix
outputs.desc: Cross-correlation between sensor noise terms

process: If reference data is available, compute residuals (sensor minus reference) to estimate noise.
If no reference, use Allan variance or difference-based methods on static periods.
Estimate the noise power spectrum to identify if noise is white, pink, or has specific features.
Compute cross-correlations between sensor errors to detect common-mode noise.

steps.description: Compute the optimal fusion weights for each sensor based on their noise characteristics: lower noise earns higher weight.

inputs.name: noise-profiles
inputs.desc: Each sensor's noise variance and spectral profile

outputs.name: fusion-weights
outputs.desc: Optimal weight for each sensor, possibly varying with frequency or time

outputs.name: expected-fused-variance
outputs.desc: The predicted variance of the fused estimate

process: Compute minimum-variance weights: inversely proportional to noise variance (for uncorrelated sensors).
If sensors are correlated, use the full covariance matrix for the weight calculation.
If noise profiles are frequency-dependent, compute frequency-dependent weights.
Calculate the expected variance of the fused output to confirm improvement over any single sensor.

steps.description: Fuse the sensor streams using a Kalman filter or weighted average: combine measurements at each time step with optimal gain.

outputs.name: fused-estimate
outputs.desc: The combined output signal with timestamp and value

outputs.name: fused-uncertainty
outputs.desc: Time-varying uncertainty (standard deviation) of the fused estimate

process: Initialize the state estimate from the first available measurements.
At each time step, predict the state forward (using a process model if available).
Update the prediction by incorporating each sensor's measurement with its weight.
Record the fused estimate and its uncertainty at each time step.

steps.description: Validate the fused output: compare against held-out reference data, check that uncertainty estimates are calibrated, and confirm improvement over individual sensors.

inputs.name: reference-data
inputs.desc: Held-out ground truth or independent measurement for validation

outputs.name: validation-metrics
outputs.desc: RMSE, bias, and coverage of uncertainty intervals against the reference

outputs.name: improvement-summary
outputs.desc: How much the fused output improved over each individual sensor

process: Compare the fused output to the reference data at matched time points.
Compute RMSE, mean bias, and mean absolute error.
Check calibration: what fraction of reference values fall within the stated uncertainty bounds.
Compare fused RMSE to each individual sensor's RMSE to quantify improvement.

steps.description: Compile the sensor fusion report: sensor characterization, fusion method, validation results, and deployment recommendations.

outputs.name: fusion-report
outputs.desc: Structured report of the entire fusion pipeline

outputs.name: deployment-config
outputs.desc: Sensor weights and filter parameters for production deployment

process: Summarize each sensor's noise profile and its contribution to the fused output.
Describe the fusion method (weighted average, Kalman, or extended Kalman) and its parameters.
Present the validation results and the improvement over individual sensors.
Provide the filter configuration for deployment: weights, process noise, measurement noise.

description: Distill raw experimental findings into structured scientific prose: extract claims from data, organize into a logical argument, draft each section (abstract, methods, results, discussion), and check internal consistency.

steps.description: Extract the factual claims supported by the data: each claim is a statement with its supporting evidence, effect size, and confidence level.

inputs.name: experimental-results
inputs.desc: Tables, figures, and statistical outputs from the experiment

inputs.name: research-question
inputs.desc: The original question the experiment addressed

outputs.name: claim-list
outputs.desc: Each claim with its evidence, effect size, p-value or CI, and strength label

outputs.name: unsupported-observations
outputs.desc: Observations in the data that do not yet map to a testable claim

process: Scan each figure and table for results that answer the research question.
For each result, write the claim as a declarative sentence.
Attach the supporting statistic: effect size, confidence interval, and p-value.
Rate the claim strength: definitive (p < 0.001 and large effect), moderate, or suggestive.

steps.description: Organize the claims into a logical argument structure: which claim comes first, what transitions connect them, and what the overall narrative arc is.

outputs.name: argument-outline
outputs.desc: Ordered list of claims with transition logic and section assignments

outputs.name: narrative-arc
outputs.desc: One-sentence summary of the story: question, approach, answer

process: Group claims by the sub-question they address.
Order groups to follow the logic: from setup to primary finding to secondary findings to implications.
Identify the transitions between groups: causal, contrastive, or additive.
Assign each claim group to the appropriate section (results vs. discussion).

steps.description: Draft the methods section: enough detail for replication, organized by procedure not by chronology, with all parameters specified.

inputs.name: experimental-results
inputs.desc: Raw data and analysis outputs for cross-reference

inputs.name: protocol-notes
inputs.desc: Lab notebook entries, SOPs, and analysis scripts used

outputs.name: methods-draft
outputs.desc: Complete methods section text

outputs.name: replication-checklist
outputs.desc: Every parameter, reagent, and setting needed to replicate

process: Organize by procedure type: participants/samples, materials, protocol, analysis.
For each procedure, specify every parameter (concentrations, temperatures, durations, software versions).
Reference established protocols by citation rather than re-describing them in full.
Check that every analysis mentioned in the results has its method described here.

steps.description: Draft the results section: present each claim in order with its supporting data, referencing figures and tables, without interpretation.

outputs.name: results-draft
outputs.desc: Complete results section text with figure and table references

outputs.name: figure-table-callouts
outputs.desc: Ordered list of which figure/table is cited where

process: Write each claim as a topic sentence, followed by the supporting statistic.
Reference the appropriate figure or table in parentheses after the statistic.
Use transitional phrases to connect claims within each sub-question.
Avoid interpretation: save 'why' for the discussion, keep results to 'what'.

steps.description: Draft the discussion section: interpret the findings, compare with existing literature, acknowledge limitations, and state implications.

outputs.name: discussion-draft
outputs.desc: Complete discussion section text

outputs.name: limitation-list
outputs.desc: Each limitation with its potential impact on the conclusions

process: Open with the main finding restated in the context of the original question.
Compare each finding with existing literature: consistent, extends, or contradicts.
Present limitations honestly, noting which conclusions they do and do not affect.
Close with implications: what should change in the field or in practice.

steps.description: Distill the entire paper into a structured abstract: background, objective, methods, results, and conclusion in the word limit.

inputs.name: discussion-draft
inputs.desc: Discussion section for the main conclusion

outputs.name: abstract-text
outputs.desc: The abstract within the specified word limit

outputs.name: keyword-list
outputs.desc: Keywords for indexing

process: Write one sentence of background establishing why the question matters.
State the objective in one sentence.
Summarize the methods in one to two sentences (design, sample, main analysis).
State the primary result with its key statistic.
Close with the main conclusion and its implication.

steps.description: Check the manuscript for internal consistency: numbers match between text and figures, methods cover every analysis, and claims in the abstract appear in the results.

outputs.name: consistency-report
outputs.desc: List of discrepancies found between sections

outputs.name: revision-checklist
outputs.desc: Items to fix before submission

process: Extract every number from the results and check it appears correctly in the abstract and figures.
Verify that every analysis in the results has its method described.
Check that every claim in the abstract has a corresponding result in the results section.
Flag any claim in the discussion not supported by a result in the results section.

description: Characterize an enzyme's kinetics: collect initial rate data, fit the Michaelis-Menten model, determine Km and Vmax, identify inhibition type, test for cooperativity, and produce the kinetic profile.

steps.description: Extract initial reaction rates from progress curves: identify the linear phase, compute the slope, and flag curves where the linear phase is too short.

inputs.name: progress-curves
inputs.desc: Product or substrate concentration vs. time for each substrate concentration

inputs.name: assay-conditions
inputs.desc: Enzyme concentration, temperature, pH, buffer composition

outputs.name: rate-table
outputs.desc: Substrate concentration and initial rate (v0) for each condition

outputs.name: linearity-report
outputs.desc: Duration of the linear phase for each curve and any flagged conditions

process: For each progress curve, identify the initial linear region (before >10% substrate depletion).
Fit a line to the linear region and extract the slope as v0.
Flag curves where the linear region is shorter than 3 time points.
Record assay conditions (temperature, pH) alongside each rate.

steps.description: Fit the Michaelis-Menten equation to the initial rate data: estimate Km and Vmax by nonlinear regression.

inputs.name: fitting-method
inputs.desc: Nonlinear least squares, Lineweaver-Burk, or Eadie-Hofstee for comparison

outputs.name: mm-parameters
outputs.desc: Km and Vmax with standard errors and confidence intervals

outputs.name: mm-fit-quality
outputs.desc: R-squared, residual plot, and whether the MM model is adequate

process: Fit v = Vmax * [S] / (Km + [S]) using nonlinear least squares.
Estimate standard errors and confidence intervals for Km and Vmax.
Optionally produce a Lineweaver-Burk plot for visual diagnosis.
Check the fit quality: are residuals random, or is there systematic curvature?

steps.description: If inhibitor data is present, determine the inhibition type: competitive, uncompetitive, noncompetitive, or mixed, by comparing fits.

inputs.name: rate-table
inputs.desc: Rates at multiple substrate and inhibitor concentrations

inputs.name: mm-parameters
inputs.desc: Uninhibited Km and Vmax as baseline

outputs.name: inhibition-type
outputs.desc: The identified inhibition mechanism with Ki

outputs.name: inhibition-evidence
outputs.desc: Model comparison (AIC/F-test) and diagnostic plots supporting the assignment

process: Fit competitive, uncompetitive, noncompetitive, and mixed inhibition models to the data.
Compare models using AIC or the extra-sum-of-squares F-test.
Check diagnostic patterns: Lineweaver-Burk lines converging at y-axis (competitive) vs. x-axis (uncompetitive).
Report Ki and the inhibition type with the model comparison evidence.

steps.description: Test for cooperative binding using the Hill equation: estimate the Hill coefficient and determine if the enzyme shows positive, negative, or no cooperativity.

inputs.name: rate-table
inputs.desc: Rates across a wide substrate range

inputs.name: mm-fit-quality
inputs.desc: Whether the standard MM model showed systematic deviations

outputs.name: hill-parameters
outputs.desc: Hill coefficient (n), K0.5, and Vmax from the Hill equation fit

outputs.name: cooperativity-verdict
outputs.desc: Whether cooperativity is present and its type (positive if n>1, negative if n<1)

process: Fit the Hill equation: v = Vmax * [S]^n / (K0.5^n + [S]^n).
Compare the Hill model fit to the standard MM model fit using AIC.
If n is significantly different from 1, classify as positive (n>1) or negative (n<1) cooperativity.
Plot log(v / (Vmax - v)) vs. log[S] to visualize the Hill coefficient graphically.

steps.description: Compile the complete kinetic profile: Km, Vmax, kcat, catalytic efficiency, inhibition parameters, and cooperativity, with all supporting evidence.

outputs.name: kinetic-profile
outputs.desc: Complete kinetic characterization document

outputs.name: comparison-table
outputs.desc: Parameters formatted for comparison with literature values

process: Calculate kcat from Vmax and enzyme concentration.
Calculate catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km) and compare to the diffusion limit.
Compile all kinetic parameters into a single table.
Compare with published values for the same enzyme or enzyme family.

description: Analyze chromatographic data: detect peaks, integrate areas, identify compounds, assess separation quality, quantify concentrations, and produce the analytical report.

steps.description: Detect and subtract the chromatographic baseline: remove drift, compensate for gradient effects, and produce a flat baseline for integration.

inputs.name: method-parameters
inputs.desc: Gradient profile, detector type, and expected baseline behavior

outputs.name: corrected-chromatogram
outputs.desc: Signal with baseline subtracted

outputs.name: baseline-trace
outputs.desc: The estimated baseline for quality review

process: Identify peak-free regions of the chromatogram for baseline anchoring.
Fit a smooth curve (polynomial, spline, or asymmetric least squares) through the anchor points.
Subtract the fitted baseline from the raw signal.
Verify the corrected signal is centered at zero in peak-free regions.

steps.description: Detect peaks in the corrected chromatogram: locate starts, apexes, and ends, then integrate the area under each peak.

inputs.name: detection-parameters
inputs.desc: Minimum peak height, minimum area, and slope sensitivity

outputs.name: peak-list
outputs.desc: Each peak with retention time, height, area, width, symmetry factor, and plate count

outputs.name: integration-report
outputs.desc: Integration events (peak start, apex, end, split, shoulder) for each peak

process: Detect peak starts and ends using slope threshold or derivative methods.
Locate the apex (maximum) of each detected peak.
Integrate the area between start and end using trapezoidal or Simpson's rule.
Compute peak shape parameters: asymmetry factor, tailing factor, and theoretical plates.

steps.description: Identify compounds by matching retention times to standards, or by retention index, or by spectral library matching if spectral data is available.

inputs.name: reference-library
inputs.desc: Standard retention times, retention indices, or spectral library

outputs.name: identified-peaks
outputs.desc: Each peak with its compound assignment and confidence level

outputs.name: unidentified-peaks
outputs.desc: Peaks that could not be matched with sufficient confidence

process: Match each peak's retention time to the reference library within a tolerance window.
If retention indices are available, compute and match indices for temperature-independent identification.
If spectral data (UV, MS) is available, use library matching with a similarity score.
Assign confidence levels: confirmed (standard + spectrum), probable (retention time only), unknown.

steps.description: Assess the quality of the chromatographic separation: resolution between critical pairs, plate count, peak capacity, and system suitability.

outputs.name: separation-metrics
outputs.desc: Resolution between adjacent peaks, plate count, peak capacity

outputs.name: suitability-verdict
outputs.desc: Pass/fail against system suitability criteria

process: Compute resolution (Rs) between every adjacent peak pair.
Identify critical pairs (Rs < 2.0) that may need method adjustment.
Calculate the average plate count and peak capacity of the column.
Check system suitability criteria: replicate precision, plate count, tailing factor limits.

steps.description: Quantify compound concentrations from peak areas using external or internal standard calibration curves.

inputs.name: identified-peaks
inputs.desc: Peaks with their compound assignments and areas

inputs.name: calibration-data
inputs.desc: Standard concentrations and their peak areas, or internal standard response factors

outputs.name: concentration-table
outputs.desc: Each compound with its calculated concentration and uncertainty

outputs.name: calibration-quality
outputs.desc: Calibration curve fit, linearity range, LOD, and LOQ

process: Fit calibration curves (linear or weighted linear) for each target compound.
Check linearity over the calibration range (R-squared, residual pattern).
Calculate the concentration of each identified peak from its area and the calibration curve.
Estimate the limit of detection (LOD) and limit of quantification (LOQ) from the calibration.

steps.description: Compile the chromatographic analysis report: method summary, chromatogram figure, peak table, identification, quantification, and system suitability.

outputs.name: chromatography-report
outputs.desc: Structured analytical report

outputs.name: results-certificate
outputs.desc: Summary table suitable for a certificate of analysis

process: Present the annotated chromatogram with identified peaks labeled.
Include the peak table with retention time, area, identification, and concentration.
Report system suitability results and whether criteria were met.
Summarize the analytical findings in a format suitable for the intended audience.

description: Quantify features in microscopy images: preprocess, segment objects (cells, particles, structures), measure morphometric parameters, count objects, analyze spatial distributions, and produce quantified results.

steps.description: Preprocess microscopy images: correct illumination, reduce noise, and enhance contrast to prepare for segmentation.

inputs.name: raw-images
inputs.desc: Microscopy images with metadata (magnification, pixel size, channel info)

inputs.name: acquisition-parameters
inputs.desc: Microscope type, objective, exposure, and illumination source

outputs.name: preprocessed-images
outputs.desc: Corrected and enhanced images ready for segmentation

outputs.name: preprocessing-log
outputs.desc: Corrections applied: flat-field, background subtraction, denoising method

process: Apply flat-field correction to remove illumination non-uniformity.
Subtract background using a rolling-ball or morphological opening method.
Apply noise reduction (median filter, Gaussian, or non-local means) appropriate to the noise type.
Adjust contrast if needed, recording the exact transformation applied.

steps.description: Segment individual objects (cells, nuclei, particles) from the preprocessed images using thresholding, watershed, or other appropriate method.

inputs.name: segmentation-parameters
inputs.desc: Expected object size range, shape, and intensity characteristics

outputs.name: segmentation-masks
outputs.desc: Label images where each object has a unique integer ID

outputs.name: segmentation-summary
outputs.desc: Total objects detected, objects touching borders (excluded), and split/merge events

process: Choose a segmentation approach based on object characteristics (threshold, watershed, or contour-based).
Apply the segmentation and label connected components.
Split touching objects using watershed or distance-transform-based separation.
Exclude objects touching the image border and objects below the minimum size threshold.

steps.description: Measure morphometric parameters for each segmented object: area, perimeter, circularity, aspect ratio, and intensity statistics.

inputs.name: preprocessed-images
inputs.desc: Original intensity images for intensity-based measurements

outputs.name: morphometry-table
outputs.desc: Each object with all measured parameters

outputs.name: population-statistics
outputs.desc: Summary statistics (mean, SD, median) for each parameter across all objects

process: For each labeled object, measure area (in calibrated units), perimeter, and bounding box.
Compute shape descriptors: circularity, solidity, aspect ratio, and eccentricity.
Measure intensity statistics within each object: mean, median, max, min, integrated density.
Compile all measurements into a table with one row per object.

steps.description: Analyze the spatial distribution of objects: nearest-neighbor distances, clustering, and spatial density maps.

inputs.name: segmentation-summary
inputs.desc: Context about image area and border exclusions

outputs.name: spatial-statistics
outputs.desc: Nearest-neighbor distribution, Clark-Evans index, and density map

outputs.name: spatial-pattern
outputs.desc: Classification as clustered, random, or dispersed with statistical test result

process: Compute the centroid of each object.
Calculate nearest-neighbor distances for all objects.
Compute the Clark-Evans index (observed/expected NN distance) to test for clustering.
Generate a spatial density map (kernel density estimate) showing regions of high and low object density.

steps.description: If multi-channel images are available, analyze colocalization: compute Pearson's, Manders', and overlap coefficients between channels within segmented objects.

outputs.name: colocalization-metrics
outputs.desc: Per-object and population-level colocalization coefficients

outputs.name: colocalization-maps
outputs.desc: Pixel-level colocalization visualization (scatter plots, overlap images)

process: Within each segmented object, extract pixel intensities from both channels.
Compute Pearson's correlation coefficient between the two channels.
Compute Manders' M1 and M2 coefficients (fraction of each channel overlapping with the other).
Generate a scatter plot of channel 1 vs. channel 2 intensity and an overlap map.

steps.description: Produce the image quantification report: representative images, measurement distributions, spatial analysis, and statistical comparisons between groups.

outputs.name: quantification-report
outputs.desc: Structured report with figures, tables, and statistical tests

outputs.name: exportable-data
outputs.desc: Clean CSV of all measurements for downstream analysis

process: Present representative images showing the segmentation overlaid on the original.
Plot distributions of key measurements (area, intensity) as histograms or violin plots.
If comparing experimental groups, run appropriate statistical tests on each measurement.
Export all measurements as a structured CSV for external analysis tools.
